instruction: Pop-up ads are really annoying. Can you enable Chrome's pop-up blocker to prevent websites from opening unwanted pop-ups?

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y

mkdir -p /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && if [ ! -f /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences ]; then echo '{}' > /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences; fi && cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"profile":{"default_content_settings":{"popups":1}}}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to enable pop-up blocker in Chrome. The evaluator checks profile.default_content_settings.popups (1=allow, 2=block). Initial state: 1 (popups allowed). Expected state: 2 (popups blocked). Getter returns 'true' when blocked.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement to enable Chrome's pop-up blocker
Getter logic is correct: reads profile.default_content_settings.popups from Chrome preferences and returns 'true' when popups==2 (blocked), 'false' when popups==1 (allowed)
Metric (exact_match) correctly compares the getter result against expected value 'true'
Expected value handling is correct: when expected.type='rule', get_rule returns config['rules'] directly, so exact_match receives {'expected': 'true'} and accesses rules['expected']
Complete coverage: evaluator checks the only requirement in the instruction
Postconfig is appropriate: kills and reopens Chrome to ensure preferences file is flushed to disk
Initial state correctly set to popups=1 (allowed) via setup config, final state should be popups=2 (blocked)
